newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Commercial Bank share issue oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Commercial Bank share issue oversubscribed.

text.p: A new primary share issue in Kenya Commercial Bank on the Nairobi Stock Exchange has been oversubscribed, the bank and brokers said on Friday.
The issue represented the third time the government had cut its shareholding in the bank. In 1988 it offloaded 20 percent and followed this up with another 10 percent in 1990.

The basis of allotment of shares will be announced by October 25 while allotment letters, share certificates and refund cheques (for those who fail to be allotted what they applied for) will be sent from November 8.
An official at Kenya's privatisation unit said the bank had no immediate plans for another primary issue although it was "greatly encouraged" by the response to this offer.
The government had offered for sale 10 percent or 11.88 million shares of its holding in the bank at 50 shillings per share. reducing state ownership to 60 percent.
"I believe the share is oversubscribed," said Kenya Commercial Bank General Manager Ezekiel arap Bii.
A partner from a leading brokerage house said there would be oversubscription in the range of 45-50 percent while another broker said he saw "slight oversubscription".
Kenya Commercial Bank closed at 55 shillings on Thursday.
The bank posted profit before taxation at 2.054 billion shillings in the first six months of 1996 but there were no comparative figures for the same period the previous year.

The bank's profit before taxation was posted at around 3.783 billion shillings in 1995 from 2.837 billion shillings in 1994 and business experts predict that pre-tax profits will jump above 4.0 billion shillings in 1996.
An official at brokerage house Shah, Munge & Partners, who sold 6.3 million of the offered shares, said there was heavy purchasing especially from foreign portfolio investors.
At the end of 1995 Kenya Commercial Bank had 275 service outlets in Kenya, according to its share prospectuses.
The Kenya Commercial Bank shares sale followed the successful offloading of part government shareholdings in national carrier Kenya Airways and National Bank of Kenya earlier in the year.
